A B S T R A C T
Bibliometric analyses frequently encounter issues such as duplicate records, missing metadata, and inconsistent
formats, reducing reliability and efficiency. Existing solutions offer minimal assistance for automated data
integration and enrichment, requiring researchers to rely on manual efforts. This paper presents a Python-based
software solution that addresses these challenges by merging datasets from Scopus and Web of Science, per-
forming DOI-based deduplication, and enhancing metadata using APIs such as Unpaywall and Semantic Scholar.
BibexPy provides analysis-ready formats that work with VosViewer and Biblioshiny, minimizing human labor
and enhancing data quality. It enables advanced analysis like as co-citation mapping and trend identification,
promoting innovation in bibliometric research approaches.

spans.content: 2. Motivation and significance
Bibliometric analysis is increasingly being used in scientific research
to identify trends, collaborations, and future disciplines [1–7].
Numerous software tools have been developed to facilitate bibliometric
mapping and analysis, including widely recognized solutions such as
Bibliometrix (Biblioshiny) [8], VOSviewer [9], CitNetExplorer [10],
CiteSpace [11], CITation Analysis [12], BibExcel [13], SciMAT [14]
ScientoPy [15], and pyBibX [16]. Although these systems have a wide
range of capabilities, many fail to handle the essential difficulty of
comprehensively integrating bibliometric data from numerous
databases.
The Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases are among of the
most extensively utilized for bibliometric studies [17]. However, when
attempting to integrate and analyze data from multiple sources in this
manner, numerous challenges arise, including data format discrep-
ancies, missing metadata, and duplicate records. Such issues necessitate
manual effort, which might result in inconsistencies and mistakes [18].
Furthermore, differences in database structures make merging prob-
lematic. Scopus, for example, employs the "Cited-By" tag field to show
author citations, whereas WoS does the same with "Cited-Reference"
[19]. As a result, for these and other reasons, scholars frequently
investigate databases independently, which limits the breadth of their
research [20].
Using a single citation database for bibliometric analysis can reduce
the comprehensiveness and reliability of conclusions. Integrating in-
formation from several citation databases, such as Scopus and Web of
Science, is critical for obtaining more reliable findings. However, this
procedure can be time-consuming, particularly for large datasets, as it
frequently necessitates extensive manual work to tackle issues like
duplication and standardization [21,22]. Automated procedures for
combining data from Scopus and Web of Science provide a streamlined
and efficient way to improve bibliometric analysis.
BibexPy is a comprehensive solution designed to address critical
challenges in bibliometric data preparation, including dataset integra-
tion, deduplication, metadata enrichment, and format conversion. The
software seamlessly merges records from Web of Science and Scopus,
ensuring consistency across data sources. DOI-based deduplication not
only enhances reliability by removing redundant entries but also en-
riches the dataset during the process by merging complementary in-
formation from duplicates. For instance, if one record is missing an
author name or contains partial keywords, these gaps are filled by
leveraging corresponding data from the duplicate entry. As a result, the
deduplication process ensures both the removal of redundancy and the
creation of a completer and more enriched dataset. Outputs are gener-
ated in formats compatible with tools like VosViewer and Biblioshiny,
simplifying downstream analysis. For instance, the relevant information
from the deduplicated item is used to fill in the blanks in a record that
lacks an author name or has partial keywords. Consequently, the data
deduplication process produces a more comprehensive and enhanced
dataset in addition to eliminating inaccurate and missing data. In order
to facilitate analysis with the preferred tool, outputs are generated in
formats that are compatible with analysis programs like VosViewer and
Biblioshiny.
This study aims to explain in detail the contributions of BibexPy to
bibliometric data preparation processes. First, the architecture and basic
functions of the software are examined; then, these functions are dis-
cussed in detail. The operation of the software is demonstrated on a
sample dataset and the state of the data before analysis is evaluated
using the biblioshiny tool. The study also discusses the potential impact
of BibexPy on future research and highlights its value for bibliometric
analysis.
3. Software description
BibexPy is a Python-based command-line tool designed to automate
the preprocessing of bibliometric information obtained from Web of
Science (WoS) and Scopus. The software efficiently performs critical
activities such as data integration, deduplication, metadata enrichment,
and format conversion, resulting in high-quality datasets suitable for
complex bibliometric analysis. Fig. 1 depicts BibExPy’s file system
layout, showing how the software organizes data inputs, processed files,
and outputs within the workspace.

3.1. Software architecture
BibexPy, developed with Python 3.9, uses a number of powerful li
braries for processing bibliometric data. The core features of the soft-
ware are built on libraries such as "Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn and
Scipy". For environmental variable management and API integration,
"requests" and "dotenv" libraries are used. The current version of
BibexPy can be run via a command line interface that provides inter-
operability across multiple platforms without requiring a graphical
interface.
Fig. 1 illustrates the software architecture of BibexPy. The software
processes bibliometric datasets from Web of Science (".txt") and Scopus
(".csv") files by performing various transformations and computations,
thereby enriching and improving the datasets. The outputs include a
consolidated dataset ("Prefix_Bib.xlsx"), files compatible with VosViewer
("Prefix_Vos.txt"), and statistical summaries. The VosViewer-compatible
output format aligns with the original export format of Web of Science,
making it suitable for use in other bibliometric analysis software as well
The software architecture is made up of several, independent mod-
ules for data preprocessing and analysis. The data preprocessing mod-
ules perform data augmentation, metadata enrichment, and file format
conversion to provide a high-quality dataset, while the analysis modules
employ these processed datasets to generate auxiliary files and reports
suited for advanced bibliometric tools. This modular approach assures
scalability, maintainability, and flexibility, making BibexPy a depend
able solution for bibliometric data preparation. The functions of BibexPy
are further explored in the sections that follow.
3.2. Data loading and preprocessing
The data loading process begins when the user saves Scopus (.csv)
and WoS (.txt) files to the Workspace/Data directory. Before beginning
the integration and enrichment procedures, the application consolidates
these raw datasets. When multiple.csv or.txt files are provided, they are
combined into unified files called wos.txt and scopus.csv, which are
stored in the merged_raw directory. Upon successive executions with the
same data, the user is offered the option of re-merging the raw files or
using the previously merged dataset. This methodology not only assures
a more efficient preparation workflow, but it also makes the combined
raw datasets compatible with other bibliometric analysis tools.
3.3. Pipelines
The BibexPy pipeline automates sequential operations for biblio-
metric data preparation and includes modular components for different
processing processes. Each stage in the pipeline improves data quality
and makes it compatible with subsequent bibliometric technologies.
3.4. Deduplication and metadata enhanced
DOI-based matching is used to identify and delete duplicate entries,
together with a procedure known as intelligent merging. This method
integrates and consolidates overlapping data from both databases. For
example, if the keywords in one database are keyword-1, keyword-2 and
in the other keyword-1, keyword-3, the merged output will be keyword-
1, keyword-2, and keyword-3. Additionally, for records without DOIs,
duplication is eliminated by generating a unique key based on the title
and year, with special characters deleted.
3.5. API based metadata enrichment
Missing metadata fields such as abstracts, citation counts, and author
affiliations are filled in by API connection with sources such as Scopus,
Unpaywall, and Semantic Scholar. This component guarantees that
datasets are complete and ready for further studies like co-citation
mapping and trend analysis.

compatible with popular bibliometric analysis programs like as

3.7. Performance metrics
To evaluate the accuracy and completeness of enriched metadata, we
define two key metric categories: completeness metrics and quality
status levels. These metrics help assess data coverage, track improve-
ments through enrichment processes, and classify metadata quality
based on missing information.
a) Completeness Metrics: Completeness metrics measure how well
metadata fields are populated and improved after enrichment. Field
Coverage calculates the percentage of non-empty fields, indicating
overall metadata completeness. API Enrichment Rate assesses how
much the metadata quality improves after integration with external
data sources. Merge Success Rate measures the percentage of re
cords successfully combined without data loss or duplication. These
indicators ensure that metadata enrichment processes effectively
enhance data integrity.
b) Quality Status Levels: To classify metadata quality, we define six
levels based on the percentage of missing data. Excellent (0% missing
data) indicates fully complete records, while Very Good (<1%)
represents minor gaps. Good (<5%) is considered acceptable for
most analyses, whereas Acceptable (<20%) denotes moderate gaps.
Poor (<50%) suggests significant missing information, and Critical
(≥50%) indicates unreliable metadata that requires substantial
improvement. These quality status levels provide a standardized
framework for evaluating the reliability of enriched metadata.
3.8. Statistical reporting
The software generates detailed statistical summaries, including:
a) Duplication rates.
b) Metadata completeness ratios.
c) Quality metrics for enriched datasets.
d) API Based Enrichment field, source, value logs.
These reports help users assess the quality and reliability of their
processed datasets.
3.9. Automation and workflow
The "DataProcessor" class is the primary access point for users, as it
defines the pipeline phases and performs the automatic processing of
bibliometric datasets. Users start the workflow with a single command:
"python DataProcessor.py".
The pipeline assists users with project selection, optional API
enrichment, and data processing. When finished, the outputs are saved
in the specified project directory. Users can utilize these results for
bibliometric analysis or further processing in programs such as Vos-
Viewer and Biblioshiny.
3.10. Time complexity of the framework
The time complexity of BibexPy’s framework is influenced by the
size of the input datasets and the operations performed, such as dedu
plication and metadata enrichment. Key factors affecting time
complexity include:
a) Scalability: The pipeline efficiently processes both small and large
datasets.
b) API Integration: Metadata enrichment through API calls depends on
the response times of external services.
c) Computational Efficiency: BibexPy is optimized for performance
using efficient algorithms for deduplication and data transformation.
Overall, BibexPy balances computational efficiency with data qual-
ity, providing researchers with a scalable solution for bibliometric data
preparation.
4. Illustrative examples
The BibexPy framework offers multiple ways for users to interact
with it, ensuring flexibility and ease of use. These options include:
a) Command-Line Interface (CLI): The command-line interface is the
principal interaction technique, allowing users to run the software
with minimal effort. Listing 1 shows an example of using the CLI to
process bibliometric datasets. Users launch the main script (python
DataProcessor.py) and follow the prompts to choose a project, set up
metadata enrichment, and generate output.
b) Python API: Advanced users can use BibexPy’s modular architecture
to directly access its classes and methods from Python programs. This
enables greater flexibility and integration with other workflows.
c) Script-Based Customization: The most flexible method to use
BibexPy is to create short Python scripts that make use of its modular
components. This technique enables greater customization and
experimentation with other workflows.
Listing 2 is an example of a Python script that shows how to use
BibexPy to process bibliometric datasets. The script begins by loading
the essential modules from BibexPy, which prepares the environment for
data processing. The first stage is loading and merging datasets from
Web of Science and Scopus into a single format using the DataImporter
class.
The next step is deduplication, which uses the Deduplicator module
to remove redundant items based on DOI matches. The script then uses
the MetadataEnricher class to add missing properties like abstracts,
author affiliations, and citation counts via API.
Finally, the FormatConverter module changes the data to a format
that VosViewer and Biblioshiny can understand. The script automates
every stage of bibliometric data preparation, resulting in a clean,
enhanced dataset that is ready for analysis. This programmatic method
allows researchers to construct custom workflows, adjust parameters,
and expand the pipeline to meet specific bibliometric study objectives.
5. Impact
BibexPy has cleared the path for comprehensive bibliometric
research by enabling the rapid integration and processing of datasets
from many sources, including Web of Science and Scopus. This capacity
enables academics to investigate problems that were previously
restricted by the limitations of manual data preparation, such as map-
ping research patterns across disciplines, assessing worldwide citation
networks, and finding emergent study areas across domains [23,24]. By
automating data integration, deduplication, and metadata enrichment,
BibexPy facilitates the pursuit of current research issues [25–27]. It
improves the reliability and comprehensiveness of bibliometric datasets,
ensuring that analyses are based on high-quality data, and decreases
preprocessing time dramatically, allowing researchers to focus on
interpretation and insight generation.
Although BibexPy is in its early stages of development, significan
efficiency gains have been observed in initial tests with sample datasets.
The results obtained in these tests clearly demonstrate the software’s
impact and potential in bibliometric data preparation processes. As the
software becomes more widely known and adopted, download statistics,
citations in academic publications, and feedback from the user com-
munity will provide more comprehensive evidence of BibexPy’s impact.

The "DataProcessor" class is the primary access point for users, as it
defines the pipeline phases and performs the automatic processing of
bibliometric datasets. Users start the workflow with a single command:
"python DataProcessor.py".
The pipeline assists users with project selection, optional API
enrichment, and data processing. When finished, the outputs are saved
in the specified project directory. Users can utilize these results for
bibliometric analysis or further processing in programs such as Vos-
Viewer and Biblioshiny.
3.10. Time complexity of the framework
The time complexity of BibexPy’s framework is influenced by the
size of the input datasets and the operations performed, such as dedu
plication and metadata enrichment. Key factors affecting time
complexity include:
a) Scalability: The pipeline efficiently processes both small and large
datasets.
b) API Integration: Metadata enrichment through API calls depends on
the response times of external services.
c) Computational Efficiency: BibexPy is optimized for performance
using efficient algorithms for deduplication and data transformation.
Overall, BibexPy balances computational efficiency with data qual-
ity, providing researchers with a scalable solution for bibliometric data
preparation.
4. Illustrative examples
The BibexPy framework offers multiple ways for users to interact
with it, ensuring flexibility and ease of use. These options include:
a) Command-Line Interface (CLI): The command-line interface is the
principal interaction technique, allowing users to run the software
with minimal effort. Listing 1 shows an example of using the CLI to
process bibliometric datasets. Users launch the main script (python
DataProcessor.py) and follow the prompts to choose a project, set up
metadata enrichment, and generate output.
b) Python API: Advanced users can use BibexPy’s modular architecture
to directly access its classes and methods from Python programs. This
enables greater flexibility and integration with other workflows.
c) Script-Based Customization: The most flexible method to use
BibexPy is to create short Python scripts that make use of its modular
components. This technique enables greater customization and
experimentation with other workflows.
Listing 2 is an example of a Python script that shows how to use
BibexPy to process bibliometric datasets. The script begins by loading
the essential modules from BibexPy, which prepares the environment for
data processing. The first stage is loading and merging datasets from
Web of Science and Scopus into a single format using the DataImporter
class.
The next step is deduplication, which uses the Deduplicator module
to remove redundant items based on DOI matches. The script then uses
the MetadataEnricher class to add missing properties like abstracts,
author affiliations, and citation counts via API.
Finally, the FormatConverter module changes the data to a format
that VosViewer and Biblioshiny can understand. The script automates
every stage of bibliometric data preparation, resulting in a clean,
enhanced dataset that is ready for analysis. This programmatic method
allows researchers to construct custom workflows, adjust parameters,
and expand the pipeline to meet specific bibliometric study objectives.
5. Impact
BibexPy has cleared the path for comprehensive bibliometric
research by enabling the rapid integration and processing of datasets
from many sources, including Web of Science and Scopus. This capacity
enables academics to investigate problems that were previously
restricted by the limitations of manual data preparation, such as map-
ping research patterns across disciplines, assessing worldwide citation
networks, and finding emergent study areas across domains [23,24]. By
automating data integration, deduplication, and metadata enrichment,
BibexPy facilitates the pursuit of current research issues [25–27]. It
improves the reliability and comprehensiveness of bibliometric datasets,
ensuring that analyses are based on high-quality data, and decreases
preprocessing time dramatically, allowing researchers to focus on
interpretation and insight generation.
Although BibexPy is in its early stages of development, significan
efficiency gains have been observed in initial tests with sample datasets.
The results obtained in these tests clearly demonstrate the software’s
impact and potential in bibliometric data preparation processes. As the
software becomes more widely known and adopted, download statistics,
citations in academic publications, and feedback from the user com-
munity will provide more comprehensive evidence of BibexPy’s impact.

all critical metadata fields were enriched and standardized, producing a
comprehensive dataset suitable for advanced bibliometric analysis.

and 2) establish a reliable foundation, API-based enrichment (Stage 3) is

6. Conclusions
BibexPy facilitates the preprocessing of bibliometric data by
enabling the creation of comprehensive and integrated datasets. It aims
to enhance the reliability and accuracy of bibliometric research by
merging data from multiple sources. In this process, critical tasks such as
duplicate record removal and missing data completion have been opti-
mized to minimize manual effort. Consequently, researchers can
conduct bibliometric analyses more efficiently and systematically.
The flexible structure of BibexPy allows for continuous updates,
ensuring that the software adapts to evolving research needs. It en-
hances the accessibility of bibliometric research and supports the
development of new data-driven methodologies. Currently, BibexPy
operates with full efficiency using Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus,
while also supporting PubMed, Dimensions, Cochrane, Lens, and
B.C. Kara et al.

6. Conclusions
BibexPy facilitates the preprocessing of bibliometric data by
enabling the creation of comprehensive and integrated datasets. It aims
to enhance the reliability and accuracy of bibliometric research by
merging data from multiple sources. In this process, critical tasks such as
duplicate record removal and missing data completion have been opti-
mized to minimize manual effort. Consequently, researchers can
conduct bibliometric analyses more efficiently and systematically.
The flexible structure of BibexPy allows for continuous updates,
ensuring that the software adapts to evolving research needs. It en-
hances the accessibility of bibliometric research and supports the
development of new data-driven methodologies. Currently, BibexPy
operates with full efficiency using Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus,
while also supporting PubMed, Dimensions, Cochrane, Lens, and
OpenAlex. However, these additional databases are still in the experi
mental phase, and their performance will be further optimized in future
updates to ensure seamless integration and usability. Future updates to
BibexPy may expand its supported data sources and provide more
customized solutions tailored to user needs. The integration of advanced
data processing techniques and machine learning applications could
facilitate a wide range of analyses, from citation network studies to text
mining.
Furthermore, incorporating big data analytics, natural language
processing (NLP), and AI-based predictive algorithms into BibexPy
could introduce significant innovations in bibliometric analysis. Inter-
active visualization tools and an optional graphical user interface may
further enhance the user experience and improve accessibility. In this
trajectory, BibexPy has the potential to evolve beyond a mere pre-
processing tool for bibliometric analysis and become a comprehensive
data analytics platform that shapes the broader landscape of scientific
research.
